core_obligations: Comparison of the two chosen sets (proof lines 1575-1582): the hypothesis says that every covering in the ambient class is combinatorially equivalent to coverings in each of the two chosen sets; applied to the members of either chosen set this produces combinatorial equivalences between the two sets in both directions, and the cited results give the equality of the categories of sheaves.
proof_roadmap: Apply the hypothesis to the members of the first chosen set to obtain combinatorial equivalences with the second.
Do the same with the roles reversed.
Conclude equality of the categories of sheaves from the cited comparison results.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that two subsets of a class of coverings satisfying the axioms of a site give the same category of sheaves, provided every covering of the ambient class is combinatorially equivalent to coverings in each of the two subsets (statement lines 1559-1573). The proof is a short but complete derivation: the hypothesis, applied to the members of either subset, gives combinatorial equivalences between the two subsets in both directions, and the cited comparison results then give the equality of the categories of sheaves (proof lines 1575-1582). The non-formal content is the two applications of the hypothesis. The claim is H1: a short derivation with each input named.
